plan.notes: Source: official University of Kansas Academic Catalog, 2026-2027 (live, non-archive catalog page), 'Bachelor of Science in Computer Science,' School of Engineering, Department of Electrical Engineering & Computer Science, transcribed by hand from the catalog's official 'Computer Science 4-Year Graduation Plan' on 2026-09-30 from https://catalog.ku.edu/engineering/electrical-engineering-computer-science/bs-computer-science/bs-computer-science.pdf. All course codes, titles, and credit hours are verbatim from the official plan; 126 credit hours across 8 semesters (Fall Year 1 through Spring Year 4: 15+15+15+17+16+18+15+15 = 126), matching the catalog's stated 126-hour requirement. Course titles for required courses are from the catalog's Degree Requirements tables on the same page; PHIL 375 title 'Moral Issues in Computer Technology' is from the official KU Philosophy catalog (Core 34 list). The catalog calls the 4-year layout a 'recommended 4-year plan... enrollment, but may vary according to existing credits' — students must work with an academic advisor. Upper Level Eligibility (ULE): EECS undergraduates must earn C or better in EPHX 210; MATH 125, 126, 127, 290; and EECS 101, 140, 168, 210, 268, 348 before enrolling in upper-level EECS courses beyond the ULE list (exceptions: EECS 312, 330, 361, 388 may be taken while completing ULE). Per-slot prerequisites are not published in the sample plan, so prereq arrays are intentionally left empty — consult the official catalog course pages and an advisor. MATH 125 is the required 'math pathway' course; starting below it extends the degree beyond 4 years. Last 30 credit hours must be completed at KU. Degree is ABET-accredited (per KU transfer guidance).
